about: The pilot's checklist notebook's own pages and places (modern-iaf/docs/training.md §11): the radio frequencies by base, the calls, the landing, weapons (each step's key record of data/keys.json) and emergency pages by jet family (f16: the Sufa and the Barak; f35i), the stowed board's place on the right thigh in each 3D cockpit's frame, and the gauge each start-up step watches. The start-up and taxi / take-off pages come from the missions' training data. Read by modern-iaf/flight/kneeboard.gd.

sources.radio: invented: every other frequency (no published military frequency found)
sources.pages.f16.weapons: the F-16 cockpit's switch places as the 3D cockpit draws them (ST STA on the AVIONIC POWER panel, MASTER ARM on the MISC panel); the keys are the sim's key table (data/keys.json); the steps are the shared weapons code's (docs/weapons.md)
sources.pages.f16.emergency: the hot start after the T.O. checklist (training.md [^ep], weak); the fire on the ground and the ejection inferred; the in-flight emergencies T.O. GR1F-16CJ-1 section III: the take-off fire and the fire p. 3-61, the air start pp. 3-79 and 3-80, the hydraulic systems p. 3-123, the generators pp. 3-43 and 3-44, STBY GAIN p. 3-108 (modern-iaf/docs/training.md §15)
sources.pages.f35i.emergency: inferred from the F-16's procedures; the straight-in landing with a flight control fault, the AFI's paragraph 7.4.3; GEAR FAIL the Eielson board's lesson (research/training.md §3.4) (modern-iaf/docs/training.md §15)
sources.stowed: inferred: on the right thigh, as the mock-up of 2026-11-13
sources.gauges: the F-16 model's RPM gauge: anim069, its needle on engines/engine[0]/n2 (f16.json animations); the dial's radius measured on a render (2026-11-15; until then anim067, the NOZ POS gauge above it)

footnotes.oa_llrd: OurAirports, Ramat David Airbase (LLRD), frequencies, https://ourairports.com/airports/LLRD/
